title: M/s R.D. Papers Ltd. v. Dakshinanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd.
coram: Shekhar B. Saraf, J.; Praveen Kumar Giri, J.
disposition: Writ dismissed; additional security demand under clause 4.20 held not bad.
headnote: The Allahabad High Court dismissed a consumer's writ seeking to quash a demand for additional security under clause 4.20 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005. Following M/s Dev Prayag Paper Mill (Pvt.) v. State of U.P. (Writ-C No. 30898 of 2016, 21 March 2017), the Court held that a distribution licensee's demand of additional security is not bad, and dismissed the petition for the reasons given in that judgment.
facts: M/s R.D. Papers Ltd. challenged a demand notice dated 21 December 2013 issued by Dakshinanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. requiring additional security under clause 4.20 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005. A Division Bench on 15 January 2014 connected the writ with Writ Petition (C) No. 51884 of 2009 and, following an interim order in M/s Supreme Ceramics Limited, restrained the respondents from demanding additional security until further orders. The petition remained pending through a 2023 listing and was finally heard in August 2025.

holding_units.holding: A distribution licensee's demand of additional security under clause 4.20 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 is not bad. A writ to quash such a demand is dismissed on the reasoning of M/s Dev Prayag Paper Mill (Pvt.) v. State of U.P.
